newsitem.title: CANADA: United Grain Growers board to meet on poison pill Thursday-UGG.
newsitem.headline: United Grain Growers board to meet on poison pill Thursday-UGG.

text.p: United Grain Growers Ltd directors will meet Thursday to discuss whether to initiate a massive dilution of its 12.5 million limited common voting shares, UGG's chief executive told Reuters on Tuesday.
"The board will be meeting Thursday morning. We think this is precedent setting," UGG chief executive Brian Hayward said.

Manitoba Court of Queen's Bench Justice John Scollin ruled earlier Tuesday that a C$172 million hostile takeover bid by rival grain handlers Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators triggered the poison pill.
The Pools withdrew their takeover bid shortly afterwards.
UGG's board of directors adopted a shareholder rights plan Feb 14 granting any shareholder other than a hostile bidder the option to purchase 8.5 more shares for each one already held at C$5.88 each.
Canadian lawyers as well as equity and commodity analysts have said they cannot recall any instance where a massive dilution of shares has occured in Canada.

More than 19 million new limited common voting shares in UGG would be added to the market if all eligible shareholders opt to buy more stock, a Pool consultant has said. The Pools said their share would be diluted to 2.0 from 14.98 percent.
UGG stock traded at C$14.05 on the Toronto Stock Exchange with 10,568 shares changing hands before trade was halted at 1234 EST/1734 GMT. The Pools' bid was at C$13.75 a share.
"The Rights Plan was put in place to protect our shareholders against an unfair creeping takeover such as this one," UGG president Ted Allen said in a statement.
"The Pools knew the details of our plan before they launched this hostile takeover. They knew what they were getting into," Allen added.
